## Follow a scan branch

A scan tree follows the acquisition references recorded by the instrument.
This kynurenine run contains a survey scan, 966, followed by three successive
fragmentation stages along one branch. To work with a large file, select scans
of interest using `Spectra::filterPrecursorScan()` before reading peak arrays.

```{r load}
library(msPurity)
file <- system.file("extdata", "msn-standards", "msPurity_L_kynurenine_161166_MSn.mzML.gz",
                    package = "msPurity", mustWork = TRUE)
spectra <- Spectra::Spectra(file, source = Spectra::MsBackendMzR(),
                           BPPARAM = BiocParallel::SerialParam())
four <- spectra[match(c(966L, 977L, 985L, 987L), Spectra::acquisitionNum(spectra))]
scans <- massSpectralTrees(four)
children <- subsetTree(scans, scan = 977L, mode = "out", depth = 1L)
children$nodes[, c("acquisitionNum", "msLevel")]
```

For a tree containing several runs, supply the run identifier with the scan
number. To retain the immediate acquisition parent in a downstream branch,
set `includeParent = TRUE`.

## Search measured peaks and candidate neutral losses

With raw spectra, a precursor–fragment tree matches each isolation m/z
to a measured peak in its acquisition parent. The default window is ±5 ppm. Supply `ppm` and
`tolerance` (Da) to change the window. If the parent peak is missing or
ambiguous, the fragment still has a link with a missing measured precursor m/z.

```{r links}
peaks <- precursorFragmentTrees(scans, spectra = four)
links <- fragmentLinks(peaks)
within_ppm <- function(x, target, ppm = 5) abs(x - target) <= target * ppm / 1e6
precursors <- subset(links, within_ppm(precursor_mz, 146.05989))
fragments <- subset(links, within_ppm(fragment_mz, 118.10124))
fragments[, c("precursor_scan", "precursor_peak", "fragment_scan", "fragment_peak")]
```

Each row is a direct link between two peak occurrences. `delta_mz` equals
the measured precursor m/z minus the measured fragment m/z. For a series
assumed to retain the same single charge and adduct, a difference near
18.010565 is consistent with a neutral loss of 18.010565 Da. Set a separate
absolute tolerance for this search. If both ions retain the same known charge
of greater magnitude, multiply `delta_mz` by that magnitude before comparing
with a target in Da. The mass agreement alone cannot identify the lost species.

```{r loss}
loss_hits <- subset(links, abs(delta_mz - 18.010565) <= 0.002)
loss_hits[, c("precursor_mz", "fragment_mz", "delta_mz", "source", "target")]
# Restrict the loss search to a particular measured precursor.
subset(loss_hits, within_ppm(precursor_mz, 209.09215),
       select = c(precursor_scan, precursor_peak, fragment_scan, fragment_peak))
```

## Use the parent peak recorded by purityA {#recorded-parent-peaks}

Pass the whole `purityA` result to `precursorFragmentTrees()` to reuse the
peak selected during each MS³ or MS⁴ purity assessment. The `ppm` argument
applies when the tree has to find a peak by m/z. An assessment that could
not identify a peak keeps its recorded status.

```{r assess-peaks, results='hide'}
pa <- purityA(spectra, msLevel = 2:4, cores = 1L, plotP = FALSE)
```

```{r compare-peak-assignments}
raw_peaks <- precursorFragmentTrees(spectra)
pa_peaks <- precursorFragmentTrees(pa)
child <- c(977L, 987L, 1053L)
raw <- raw_peaks$selections[match(child, raw_peaks$selections$acquisitionNum), ]
assessed_peaks <- pa_peaks$selections[match(child, pa_peaks$selections$acquisitionNum), ]
data.frame(child, raw_peak = raw$parent_peak_index, raw_status = raw$match_status,
           pa_peak = assessed_peaks$parent_peak_index, pa_mz = assessed_peaks$measured_mz,
           pa_source = assessed_peaks$assignment_source)
```

For scan **977**, only the raw file contains the peaks of survey scan **966**.
Both inputs identify peak **44** in scan **985** as the precursor of scan **987**.
For scan **1053**, the instrument targeted m/z **174.05460**. The assessment
selected peak **15** in scan **1047** at m/z **174.05566**, about **6.14 ppm**
from the target. The default raw search leaves that assignment unresolved.
The PA tree uses peak 15 for all 16 products.

Trace one product of scan 1053 back to the measured precursor. The edge
points from the parent peak to the fragment.

```{r recorded-peak-branch, eval=requireNamespace("igraph", quietly = TRUE), fig.width=6, fig.height=3}
product <- subset(fragmentLinks(pa_peaks), fragment_scan == 1053 & fragment_peak == 1L)
parent_pair <- subsetTree(pa_peaks, node = product$target, mode = "in", depth = 1L)
labels <- with(parent_pair$nodes,
    sprintf("Scan %d · peak %d\nm/z %.5f", acquisitionNum, peak_index, mz))
plot(parent_pair, labels = labels, main = "Parent peak recorded by purityA",
     vertex.label.degree = -pi / 2, vertex.label.dist = 8, vertex.label.adj = c(0.5, 0.5))
```

## Plot or export a hit

Use the exact target ID to follow a matching fragment back to its immediate
precursor. The ID distinguishes peaks with the same m/z in different scans.
Plotting, igraph conversion and GraphML export use the optional igraph package.

```{r display, eval=requireNamespace("igraph", quietly = TRUE), fig.width=6, fig.height=3}
branch <- subsetTree(peaks, node = loss_hits$target[1L], mode = "in", depth = 1L)
plot(branch)
igraph::as_edgelist(as_igraph(branch))
writeGraphML(branch, tempfile(fileext = ".graphml"))
```


## Keep passing products after filtering

`passingOnly = TRUE` uses the product flags saved by `filterFragSpectra()`.
A failed product can still be the measured precursor of a later scan.
Here, peak 44 in scan 985 supplies the two passing products of scan 987.

```{r passing-products}
filtered <- filterFragSpectra(pa, msLevel = 2:4, allfrag = TRUE,
    plim = 0.95, snr = 3, rmp = TRUE, cores = 1L)
passing <- precursorFragmentTrees(filtered, passingOnly = TRUE)
subset(fragmentLinks(passing), fragment_scan == 987,
       select = c(precursor_scan, precursor_peak, fragment_scan, fragment_peak,
                  fragment_mz, assignment_source))
```
